title: PRESSER | Yolett McPhee-McCuin (11-24-26)
text: Coach, you are are you the with all the new players, I feel like defense defense been a strength, but I I guess has has that been how tough is it to have a completely new cast and and be so cohesive on defense what from what I can tell so far? >> Well, it's definitely a challenge on both ends of the floor right now, but we're definitely ahead defensively than we are offensively. There's still some things from the defensive end that I want us to correct like boxing out and finishing the the possession. But as far as us being in the half court understanding schemes, I've I've I just told the team two days ago that I was really pleased with their connectivity, but now we need to finish it off with securing the rebound so we can get out and run. >> Kind of with that, but on the offensive side, you guys have scored a lot of points off turnovers, but sometimes the half court offense has been a little stagnant. How have you guys looked to improve that so far? >> Yeah, you know, I think we as a staff, we work really hard to try to understand our team and put them in the best situations for them to be successful. That's something that we're focusing on this week since we're not going to play in the tournament, we'll be home. Clarifying roles, getting our players to understand what we need from them and making sure that we're all on the same page. [snorts] I'd be lying if I said I hadn't been a little frustrated with with how we've been looking offensively, especially we always have it seems like we've been having one to two quarters where we just look really bad. And then we, you know, Ohio State, we played three good quarters versus A&M two good quarters. It's always like two or three, never four. So that's something that we're discussing at a high level and we're looking at and I think once the roles defined more clear and our players understand what we want them to [clears throat] what we how we want them to play and what shots are good shots and what shots are bad shots will get better. >> Does the team have any Thanksgiving plans this week or you guys just business as as normal? >> Yeah, I mean we're going to get together Thursday is an off day for us but we're going to get together and and have a meal. So at least I don't have to worry about cooking. One will be provided provided for us. Really looking forward to spending time with the team outside of basketball for sure. >> [snorts] >> How important do you think that could be as this team continues to look and find an identity on the court? How could the off off the court stuff be beneficial? >> Huge. We had a session this morning. So I do this thing with the team. I've I've just started it this year where we meet once a month and and this month was we call it the Breakfast of Champions and we all got together and we were talking about what team 52 what what they want their identity to be what that's going to look like sound like and feel like and Tanisha brought up about how you know she's been a part of winning programs Final Four when she was at South Carolina and she just talked about how connected they were off the court. And so that's something that our team has to be intentional about and this Thanksgiving provides that opportunity for us to be gone. Like I said in the presser I was sulking about it for like a month that we weren't going to Puerto Rico but now it is truly a blessing because we get to just be here and focus on us and not an opponent. >> And to look ahead to put you back on the focus of the opponent what have you seen from Memphis and who stands out to you from their squad so far? >> Yeah, first of all I'm just a big fan of Hannah Haydon the the coach. You know I just love how she coaches. I love how she gets her teams to play. Um, right now they're undefeated. They'll play tomorrow um against another pretty good uh matchup. And so they'll either come in seven and 0 or they'll come in with a loss like us. Um, I expect it to be a great game. I expect it um to be one where we have to be disciplined. They already beat an SEC opponent. Um, so I don't think that they are going to come in not confident. And uh we're going to have to really focus on being our best self. You know, right now it's very hard for me to focus on the opponent as much as I need to focus on our team. So our goal this week is to make sure we're doing the things the right way. And then obviously we'll 48 hours before the game we'll we'll prepare for the matchup. But I expect it to be a good one. >> [snorts] >> And two really big matchups kind of back-to-back with NC State just coming a couple days after. What can this next kind of stretch tell you about your team? >> Mhm. Well, I'm hoping that we we are able to see some growth, you know, some tangible things um that we're to show where we've grown. Um, and that that's going to be huge for us because now we have real numbers. We've played enough games where we can start saying, okay, we have enough data where we know like, okay, we're deficient in this. For example, our free throw shooting. We're shooting 52% you know, and no one's guarding us. So that's something that we need to focus on. It's not because they're not getting reps. They're getting reps at the free throw shooting. They're just um not focused when they're up there. Same thing with boxing out. We have the ability to box out, but we need to be focused on boxing out. So these these things we can improve. And then obviously offensively, like I said, our staff and and I we're looking at how we can set our players up to be successful. >> Broadly, oh, go ahead, Sam. Sorry. >> Uh uh broadly, now now that the team has had some time to settle, and how do you feel like Jada Richard's doing point guard role? Kind of shading at all? >> Yeah, I mentioned the other day, it's funny, it was like a firestorm. I'm not sure, you know, where that came from because um for me, I was just talking about a different role for her, and it truly is a a different role. Um she's coming along. Uh I think if you were to even ask her, she knows that she needs to um like completely understand and grasp what we need here at Ole Miss for the point guard position, and that's my job and her position coach's job to help her to understand. This is a new role. She is with a new team and uh with new expectations as far as we are concerned here because we have to have it. And uh I think she is completely bought in, but uh needs to just get comfortable with under You can't She's bought in, but you can't have complete buy-in until you really understand what is needed from the coach. And so that's one of the things that I feel like I've fell fallen short on is helping her to understand, hey, this is what we need from you here in order for us to be successful. I am excited about what it looks like once that happens um because she puts in the work. She's incredibly humble um and she's tough, so I look forward to seeing her grow in that area. >> You know, coach, I've the last couple of years I covered Deniyla at Illinois State. Just what has she brought to the table so far this season, you know, in the paint [clears throat] just as a leadership, you know, player? >> Yeah, uh you know, Niya is a diamond in the rough. Uh she is one that uh when we talked this morning, she talked about how the expectation um is different, but also is the the competition as well. And so she's really having to step up. Um I think once she gets comfortable in her new role and what we expect, uh we're even going to see her be better. Uh she had a two-week stretch where she looked like the best player on the floor. Um and now we have to get her back to that where she's confident in knowing what she's good at and bringing that every single day. But the best is for my whole team. That's one of the things that I'm incredibly thankful for is that if right now I believe our team holistically is operating at maybe a level four and 10 would be the max. So in as far as I'm concerned, there's room to grow for all of them. Thank y'all.
